Adjust visit times for Daylight Saving Time (DST) in the spring (spring forward)

Source: R/daylight_saving.R
adjust_dst_spring.Rd

This function adjusts feed or water visit times that fall during the start of Daylight Saving Time (DST) in the spring. In North America, clocks jump forward from 2:00 AM to 3:00 AM, skipping the hour between 2–3 AM. Some sensors continue recording using local time, which may result in invalid or misaligned timestamps.

Usage

adjust_dst_spring(
  data_frame,
  dst_detected_time,
  start_col = start,
  end_col = end,
  daylight_change_duration = 60
)

Arguments

data_frame

A data frame with two columns representing the start and end time of each visit, formatted as "HH:MM:SS".

dst_detected_time

A lubridate::hms object indicating the time when DST fallback starts (e.g., 01:59:00).

start_col

Name of the start time column (unquoted). Default is: start

end_col

Name of the end time column (unquoted). Default is : end

daylight_change_duration

An integer for the fallback duration in minutes (default = 60).

Value

A data frame with updated start and end time columns after adjusting for spring DST jump.

Details

The function removes visits that start before the DST jump and end during the skipped hour (2–3 AM), and shifts all visits that occur after the DST jump forward by one hour to reflect the actual (post-DST) clock time.

This function assumes North American spring DST behavior (2:00 AM → 3:00 AM), but can be adapted for other timezones with a suitable dst_detected_time and daylight_change_duration.
